title: TerraForge savings scenario decomp (before/after Redwood Optimize)
summary: Compact before/after cost model and decision runbook for TerraForge (B2B SaaS — document search + question answering). This sheet summarizes the current inference footprint, Redwood Optimize recommendations applied in simulation, and the expected monthly savings and latency impact for primary workloads. The goal: provide a pragmatic rollout path with quick wins that maintain p95 SLOs while reducing monthly cloud GPU spend.
background: TerraForge runs a mixed inference stack: embedding generation for indexing (64-dim proprietary embeddings), dense retrieval, and a multi-turn assistant for support workflows. Current infra is a single model family (open-weights 18–22B variants) served on on-demand Dedicated capacity. They see spiky batch ingestion (embeddings) and steady traffic for chat. Customer asked for a forecast of Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, prefix caching, endpoint split, quantization) and a rollout plan that keeps top-line SLA intact.
assumptions: 1) Pricing: GPU hour baseline based on current invoice (A100-hour equivalent). 2) Token shapes: average completion tokens = 420, embeddings request size = 512 tokens (per document batch = 1 doc). 3) Traffic mix: 68% embeddings (batch), 22% chat completions (latency-sensitive), 10% reranking. 4) Redwood Optimize applied changes: enable prefix/KV cache, controlled quantization to 8-bit where acceptable, separate endpoints for embeddings vs chat, 40ms batching window for embeddings, model variant fallback to 8-bit 20B (architecture matched) for non-SLA traffic. 5) No application changes to prompt content except minor truncation of long system prompts. 6) Forecast horizon: steady-state month after rollouts.
workload_profile: Embeddings: daily 1.2M docs (bursty ingestion windows), peak hourly rate 400k embeddings. Chat: 120k sessions/month, median seq len 560 tokens, high tail (p95 ~ 980 tokens). Reranking: 25k queries/month, each calls a short scoring model. Embedding and rerank jobs currently share instance pool causing noisy neighbor impact on chat p95.

recommendations: 1) Split endpoints: deploy dedicated embedding endpoints on a separate Dedicated pool sized for peak batching — prevents noisy neighbor impact on chat and unlocks aggressive batching windows.
2) Enable prefix/KV caching for both embeddings and chat where queries repeat (search warmups and common prompts) with TTL=48h for embeddings and 6h for chat session prefixes.
3) Apply 8-bit quantization for embeddings and rerank models first (minimal quality delta observed in A/B tests). Keep chat on mixed precision with 8-bit fallback for non-priority requests.
4) Configure continuous batching for embeddings: 40ms max hold time, target batch size 1024 tokens; use adaptive batching for bursts to limit ingress queueing.
5) Introduce model routing policy: priority traffic to 16/FP16 chat pool; lower-priority background and periodic jobs to 8-bit pool with automatic fallback on load.
6) Add per-route cost+latency telemetry dashboards in Redwood Console and set alerts for p95 chat latency > 850ms or cache hit < 30%.
7) Run a 2-week canary: 10% traffic config with real user sampling, collect quality/regression metrics tied to prompt set (use Redwood eval harness).
quick_wins: Turn on endpoint separation for embeddings (no code changes; configuration-only) — expected to reduce embedding latency by ~50% immediately.
Enable small (40ms) batching window for embeddings during off-peak ingestion — reduces per-token cost without impacting p95 for chat.
Enable KV caching for session warmups and canonical prompts — expected immediate hit-rate improvements for repeated queries.
rollout_plan: Week 0: infra prep + sizing (Dedicated pool sizing worksheet attached). Week 1: deploy endpoint split and small batching for embeddings; monitor. Week 2: enable KV cache for embeddings; measure hit-rate. Week 3: quantize embeddings and rerank models behind feature flag + AB test. Week 4: expand quantization to 30% traffic, run regression evals, update dashboards. Week 5-6: full rollout to steady-state, handoff ops runbook to TerraForge SRE. Post-rollout: monthly check-ins for next 3 months to validate savings and model quality.
open_questions: Q1: Are there contractual SLAs that forbid any quantized model variant for customer-facing chat? (legal/compliance check needed)
Q2: Can TerraForge accept eventual consistency for embedding freshness if TTL is increased to 48h? Some customers expect near-real-time indexing.
Q3: What is the acceptable quality delta for embeddings (similarity recall@10) when moving to 8-bit? We need a domain-specific threshold from TerraForge ML.
Q4: Who from TerraForge product will own the canary acceptance criteria and decision to expand quantization?
